summary: This note introduces Zenith Innovations' mileage reimbursement and transportation policy through a narrative about sales representative Emily. It explains eligibility, how employees log and submit mileage, the use of IRS mileage rates, and the support and review processes. It also mentions a future fleet of company vehicles that may reduce personal vehicle use.
one_line: Zenith Innovations' mileage reimbursement policy covers business use of personal vehicles at IRS rates, with daily logs, monthly submission, and support.
key_facts: Zenith Innovations reimburses mileage in line with standard IRS mileage rates.
Mileage reimbursement applies to all employees who use personal vehicles for business-related travel.
Normal commutes to an employee's usual workplace are excluded from reimbursement.
Employees log their starting odometer reading, for example with a quick note on a smartphone.
Employees complete daily travel logs each evening, recording destinations, purpose of travel, and mileage.
Logs can be kept in a mobile app or in a spreadsheet.
Travel logs are submitted at the end of each month through an online processing system.
The reimbursement approach covers out-of-pocket expenses plus depreciation and wear and tear on employees' vehicles.
Zenith Innovations anticipates a fleet of company vehicles that will in the future reduce the need for personal vehicle use.
A dedicated support team helps clarify which trips qualify and how to use the travel log app.
Zenith Innovations commits to regular assessments of its travel and expense policy, adapting to changes in regulations, technology, and employee feedback.
Emily, a sales representative, is used as the example employee traveling to meet a potential client.
